_readme: THE PROBLEM: every new opportunity needs a sentence in four languages.
Translating one by hand each week costs time; machine translation gets
deadlines and requirements subtly wrong, which is dangerous on this site.
THE SOLUTION: opportunity descriptions are highly repetitive. So the
SENTENCE PATTERNS are translated once, by a human, and reused forever.
The weekly robot only fills in the blanks — {amount}, {date}, {provider} —
and numbers, dates and proper nouns read the same in all four languages.
A new entry is therefore complete in DE / EN / FA / AR the moment it is
added, with no translation step and no machine guessing.
TO ADD A NEW PATTERN: copy a block, keep the {placeholders} identical in
all four languages, and have a speaker check the Dari and Arabic once.
After that it is reusable forever.
If a new opportunity fits NO pattern here, the robot must not invent a
sentence — it marks the entry 'needs a human sentence' and a person writes
it. That case should be rare.
